title: Exponent-Reduction Effects on MiMC Algebraic Degree
summary: Beyond the finite-field exponent threshold, exponent reduction and sparse terms can lower practical algebraic degree; predicting changed monomials and tightening bounds remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the field-based polynomial analysis of MiMC-like Feistel constructions, characterize when finite-field exponent reduction, arising once the degree exceeds $2^n-1$, changes a particular monomial, and use this characterization to tighten algebraic-degree bounds while accounting for sparse polynomial terms that can lower the practical degree. The characterization should explain cases such as $n=3$, where $(x_0\oplus k_0)^{27}(x_1\oplus k_1)^{18}\equiv(x_0\oplus k_0)^6(x_1\oplus k_1)^4$ and the algebraic degree decreases from $\operatorname{wt}(27)+\operatorname{wt}(18)=6$ to $\operatorname{wt}(6)+\operatorname{wt}(4)=4$.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of field-based polynomial models for MiMC-like Feistel constructions.
parameters: n: finite-field parameter controlling the exponent-reduction threshold and instantiated as 3 in the example
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a condition predicting which monomials change under finite-field exponent reduction and use it to tighten algebraic-degree bounds while incorporating sparsity effects.

citations.label: On the Field-Based Division Property: Applications to MiMC, Feistel MiMC and GMiMC

progress.summary: The paper gives an n=3 example in which exponent reduction lowers the algebraic degree from 6 to 4, then identifies the lack of a predictive condition and the additional degree-lowering effect of sparse terms.
citation_labels: jiamin cui et al., On the Field-Based Division Property: Applications to MiMC, Feistel MiMC and GMiMC
